description: HPO terms for the 20 lcat checklist items (configs/checklists/lcat.json), chosen on 2026-11-15 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-47 (extending D-40). 'observed' is the one term a record may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite no single term covers exactly (the free-text feature rows carry the specific term), or a broader ancestor where HPO has no term of the item's scope (explained in the note). 'excluded' lists every term a record may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

corneal opacity.note: Corneal opacity; exact name match (EXACT synonym 'Corneal clouding'); stromal opacification is a descendant.

low hdl cholesterol.note: Decreased circulating HDL-C concentration (EXACT synonyms 'Low HDL-cholesterol', 'Decreased HDL cholesterol').

low apolipoprotein a-i or a-ii.note: Composite: Decreased circulating apolipoprotein A-I concentration and Decreased circulating apolipoprotein A-II concentration; their common parent, Decreased circulating apolipoprotein concentration, is broader (it includes apoB, apoC-II and apoE), so observed is null.

hypertriglyceridemia.note: Hypertriglyceridemia; exact name match (EXACT synonym 'Increased plasma triglycerides').

elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol.note: Broader ancestor: Abnormal circulating cholesterol concentration. HPO has no term for raised plasma unesterified (free) cholesterol; Unesterified cholesterol accumulation in cultured fibroblasts (HP:6000158) is a cellular finding, and Hypercholesterolemia concerns total cholesterol, so neither is used. Nothing is excluded because the only covering term is broader than the item.

reduced cholesteryl ester fraction.note: Broader ancestor: Abnormal circulating cholesterol concentration. HPO has no term for a low esterified-to-total cholesterol fraction; Elevated circulating cholesteryl ester concentration is the opposite direction, and Low cholesterol esterification rate (HP:0003349, under Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity) measures the enzyme reaction, not the plasma fraction, so it is not used. Nothing is excluded because the only covering term is broader than the item. Review whether HP:0003349 should be accepted instead.

low ldl cholesterol or apolipoprotein b.note: Composite: Decreased circulating LDL-C concentration (EXACT 'Hypobetalipoproteinemia') and Decreased circulating apolipoprotein B concentration; neither is an ancestor of the other and their common ancestors (Hypolipoproteinemia, Abnormal circulating protein concentration) are broader, so observed is null.

lipoprotein x.note: Elevated circulating lipoprotein-X concentration; LpX is normally absent from plasma, so its presence is read as this term.

anemia.note: Anemia; exact name match. Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001878), named in the item's quotes, is a descendant.

proteinuria.note: Proteinuria; exact name match. Nephrotic range proteinuria is a descendant; Nephrotic syndrome is not.

hematuria.note: Hematuria; exact name match; microscopic and macroscopic hematuria are descendants.

nephrotic syndrome.note: Nephrotic syndrome; exact name match. It is not a descendant of Proteinuria in HPO.

chronic kidney disease or renal failure.note: Renal insufficiency (EXACT synonym 'Renal failure') covers the item: Chronic kidney disease (EXACT 'CKD'; stage 5 CKD carries the synonym 'Chronic renal failure') is its child, so the union is Renal insufficiency itself. Both terms may be excluded; Renal insufficiency also covers acute kidney injury, which a paper's 'normal renal function' rules out too.

atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.note: Atherosclerosis (EXACT synonym 'Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease'). Excluded lists the site-specific terms (Coronary artery atherosclerosis, Cerebral artery atherosclerosis, Aortic atherosclerotic lesion, Renal artery atherosclerosis, Pulmonary arterial atherosclerosis) rather than Atherosclerosis itself, because in this HPO release Foam cells, and through it Renal glomerular foam cells (HP:0032583, the 'glomerular foam cells' item), sit under Atherosclerosis: excluding Atherosclerosis would logically exclude the glomerular foam cells many FLD biopsies show. For the same reason an observed glomerular foam cell term implies Atherosclerosis by inheritance; review this.

glomerular sclerosis.note: Glomerular sclerosis; exact name match (EXACT 'Glomerulosclerosis'); Segmental and Global glomerulosclerosis, the forms the review names, are children.

mesangial expansion or mesangial lipid d.note: Mesangial matrix expansion (EXACT 'Increased glomerular mesangial matrix') covers only matrix expansion; HPO has no mesangial lipid deposit or vacuolization term, and the parent Abnormal glomerular mesangium morphology is broader (sclerosis, hypercellularity, immune deposits), so observed is null and only the expansion component can be excluded.

glomerular basement membrane thickening.note: Thickened glomerular basement membrane (EXACT 'Thickening of the glomerular basement membrane') covers the thickening; HPO has no GBM lipid deposit term (electron-dense deposit terms are not specific to lipid), and Abnormal glomerular basement membrane morphology is broader, so observed is null and only the thickening component can be excluded.

glomerular foam cells.note: Renal glomerular foam cells; exact name match. Glomerular endocapillary foam-cell hypercellularity is narrower but not a descendant, so it is listed for exclusion too. HPO places Foam cells under Atherosclerosis; see the note on 'atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease'.

podocyte foot process effacement.note: Podocyte foot process effacement; exact name match (fused foot processes read as effacement).

tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis.note: Composite: Renal tubular atrophy (EXACT 'Tubular atrophy'), Renal interstitial fibrosis and Tubulointerstitial fibrosis (the two fibrosis terms are siblings, not ancestor and descendant). Their common ancestors (e.g. Abnormal tubulointerstitial morphology, which includes nephritis) are broader, so observed is null.
